items.question: Which columns does the CSV have, and in what order and with what header names?
items.ticket: download their requisition list (with status and fill counts) as CSV
items.chose: Emits the header 'Requisition ID,Title,Status,Openings,Filled,Created', with openings and filled as separate columns.
items.instead: Use different header labels or a different column order, or include a single 'filled/openings' column or a remaining-openings column.

items.question: In what order are the rows written?
items.chose: Sorts a copy of the input by creation time ascending, then by id as a string compare.
items.instead: Keep the input order, or sort newest first.

items.question: What does the CSV contain when the list is empty?
items.chose: Returns the BOM and the header row only.
items.instead: Return an empty string, or the header without a BOM.

items.question: Does the output start with a byte-order mark?
items.chose: Prepends a UTF-8 BOM (U+FEFF) to the output.
items.instead: Emit no BOM, so the output is plain CSV text.

items.question: Which line terminator is used, and does the last row end with one?
items.chose: Ends every line, including the last, with CRLF.
items.instead: Use LF as the separator, with no trailing newline after the last row.

items.question: How are fields containing commas, quotes or line breaks escaped?
items.chose: Quotes the field per RFC 4180 and doubles any embedded quotes.
items.instead: Leave fields unquoted, or also quote fields with leading or trailing whitespace.

items.question: How is a field starting with =, +, - or @ handled, given spreadsheet formula injection?
items.chose: Writes the value as is, with no neutralising prefix.
items.instead: Prefix such values with a single quote or similar so spreadsheets do not run them as formulas.

items.question: What is written for a null or missing title?
items.instead: Write a placeholder such as '(untitled)', or throw.

items.question: How is the creation time formatted?
items.chose: Writes the full UTC ISO 8601 string from toISOString().
items.instead: Write a date-only value or a locale-formatted local time.

items.question: What happens when a row has bad data (unknown status, invalid or negative openings or filled count, filled greater than openings, invalid date)?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the requisition id, and writes no partial CSV.
items.instead: Skip the bad row, or write it as is or with the values clamped.

items.question: Which statuses are valid?
items.chose: Accepts only open, on_hold, filled and cancelled, and throws on any other value.
items.instead: Pass any status string through unchanged.

items.question: Are zero openings and filled equal to openings valid?
items.chose: Accepts openings of 0, filled of 0, and filled equal to openings.
